# `plan_review/attest.py` is at the hard cap with ZERO headroom

## Context

Landing bug c083 (untracked-tolerance on four plan-review snapshot reads) hit this immediately: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` was **799** lines on `origin/main` against the **800** hard cap enforced by `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py::test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap` (limit single-sourced in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`).

A two-call-site change — adding `ignore_untracked=True` to two existing calls — could not be landed in the natural form:

- appending the kwarg inline made the line 114 chars, over the ruff E501 limit of 100;
- wrapping the call to satisfy E501 cost +2 lines -> 801, over the cap;
- adding the explanatory comments the change deserved cost more -> 803.

It only fit by importing `collect_plan_relation_snapshot` directly (+1 line for the import, which let the call fit on one line at 95 chars), landing the file at **exactly 800** — passing only because the gate is `> limit`, with **zero** remaining headroom. The file currently sits at **794** on `origin/main`; the headroom problem is unchanged.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

The next change to this file — any change, including a one-line bug fix — cannot land without first splitting it. The cost is not paid by whoever grew the file; it is paid by whoever next needs to fix a bug in it, under time pressure, as an unrelated blocker. That is exactly the situation task `2682` was raised for when `runner.py` hit 800 in the LLM-provider-seam epic, and it was resolved there by a real call-graph split (`runner.py` 800 -> 655 + `structured_run.py`).

It also actively degrades the code: in c083 the comments explaining WHY untracked files must be tolerated had to be cut from `attest.py` and replaced with a pointer to `resign.py`, purely to save lines. The cap is now shaping documentation quality, not just structure.

## Approach — the DECIDED seam (analysis complete)

**This is a pure refactor: zero behavioral change.** No function body is rewritten; a contiguous
call-graph cluster moves to a new sibling module and is re-exported so every existing call site
and monkeypatch target keeps resolving.

**Seam chosen: the remediation-mode eligibility cluster.** Extract `remediation_mode_candidate`
and its single private helper `_sidecar_branch_decision` from `attest.py` into a new sibling
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/remediation_mode.py`.

Why this seam and not the others considered:

- It is a **pre-existing, isolated call-graph cluster**: `_sidecar_branch_decision` has exactly
  ONE caller in the entire repository — `remediation_mode_candidate`, directly above it — and
  `remediation_mode_candidate` is a call-graph LEAF within `attest.py` (nothing else in the file
  calls it). Verified with both Serena `find_referencing_symbols` and a repo-wide string `grep`.
- It is a **distinct concern**: "is this re-review eligible for the remediation floor?" — a
  Pass-3 floor input — as opposed to `attest.py`'s core job of signing attestations and computing
  claim-gate validity.
- The **drift-refresh cluster was evaluated and rejected**: `drift_refresh_candidate` calls
  `compute_validity` and `_authoritative_manifest` (which must stay in `attest.py`), and
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py` monkeypatches `attest._rehash` and then calls
  `attest.refresh_attestation`, so moving that cluster would silently break the patch seam.
  This seam has no such inward dependency.

Dynamic-reference safety (the failure mode that broke epic `061c` S1):

- `remediation_mode_candidate` is reached ONLY through the module attribute
  `attest.remediation_mode_candidate` (`plan_review/__init__.py` and four test modules), including
  a `monkeypatch.setattr(attest, "remediation_mode_candidate", ...)`. Re-exporting the moved name
  from `attest.py` keeps every one of those sites resolving unchanged.
- The moved code calls `current_material_fingerprint` and `registry_version`, both of which the
  tests monkeypatch **on the `attest` module object**
  (`monkeypatch.setattr(attest, "current_material_fingerprint", ...)`,
  `monkeypatch.setattr(attest, "registry_version", ...)`). The new module must therefore resolve
  both **through the `attest` module at call time** (`from . import attest` inside the function
  body, then `attest.<name>(...)`) — a `from .attest import <name>` would bind the original and
  silently ignore the patch. The deferred import also keeps the new module import-cycle safe
  against `attest.py`'s re-export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` is under 700 LOC (real headroom, not 799) — landed at **656** on main (094c4c4525)
- [x] any extracted module is at least 100 LOC (no sub-100-LOC fragmentation) — `remediation_mode.py` is **182**
- [x] `attest.remediation_mode_candidate` still resolves (re-exported), so no call site or
      monkeypatch target in `src/` or `tests/` changes — verified at runtime
      (`attest.remediation_mode_candidate is remediation_mode.remediation_mode_candidate` -> True)
      and by repo-wide grep: every residual reference is either prose or a live
      `attest.remediation_mode_candidate(...)` call
- [x] zero test edits are required by the move, or each required edit is justified in the commit message — **zero** test files touched; the change is 3 files, all under `src/`
- [ ] [operator-attested] the full suite passes with a test count equal to the pre-split count plus any new
      seam tests, evidenced by the two pytest summary lines quoted in a comment
